_timing: No narration yet. Each beat is the larger of the time it needs to finish animating and the time it takes to read, plus a 22-frame hold. This is a floor, not considered pacing — measure a real read and switch this topic to voiceCuts.

beats.text: Pac-Man was renamed to stop vandals scratching an F onto arcade cabinets.
beats.note: Repeated by CNN, Wikipedia, and countless retellings; but no Namco executive, document, or interview has ever been found saying this.

beats.name: Puck Man
beats.role: 22 May, Japan. Namco's original name for the character, from 'paku-paku'; the Japanese sound for a mouth opening and closing.

beats.text: The shape came from a missing slice of pizza.
beats.note: "I was eating a whole pizza while thinking about a game themed on eating," he told Game Informer in 2020, "and I came up with the design after looking at the pie with a slice taken out."

beats.name: Midway
beats.role: October. Published the US version under the changed name; Pac-Man; an Americanisation, not a confirmed scandal dodge.

beats.context: coin-operated plays between 1980 and 1999, per Guinness World Records; the highest-grossing arcade game ever.

beats.line: Nobody at Namco has ever confirmed the vandalism story.
